_meta.purpose: HISTORICAL-PROXY tier (tier 2 of 3). Pre-1816 units, where the citable relational primitives (COW CINC, ATOP, ICOW) do not exist, but established quantitative historical series DO - and are used as era-appropriate proxies.
_meta.confidence: Below the citable tier (tier 1), above pure interpretation (tier 3). Real reproducible data, but: (a) relative power is proxied by economic MASS (Maddison GDPpc x population) rather than the COW composite; (b) population is supplied from standard historical demography (NOT in the repo's Maddison GDPpc subset - see tech debt); (c) alliance/territorial-claim primitives are coded from documented historical fact, not ICOW/ATOP.
_meta.e1_method: economic_mass = GDPpc x population. own vs JOINT adversary mass.
_meta.tech_debt: Population is the weak link: the repo's longrun_pillars.json carries Maddison GDP-per-capita but NOT population. The figures below are standard historical-demography estimates (c.1770), citable to the Maddison population series / standard sources, and should be tightened to the exact Maddison population CSV when ingested. GDPpc year-gaps (Austria nearest 1820, Russia nearest 1860) are flagged per value.

Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth@1772.label: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, pre-First-Partition 1772 - the pre-1816 exogenous-erasure case, now proxy-backed

internal_pillars.provenance: P1 = V-Dem rule-of-law @1789 (vdem_longrun.json POL rol=0.18) - the nearest historical V-Dem value; captures the liberum-veto institutional paralysis IN THE DATA (cf. partitioners Prussia 0.64, Austria 0.70). NB 1789 is post-first-partition. P5 left null (no contemporaneous stability series); the relational reading does not require it for this illustration. Internal read, historical-proxy tier.

human_capital_proxy.provenance: longrun_pillars.json POL P3_literacy @1750 = 5.0 (vs Prussia/DEU 38.0) - a real human-capital gap, for context.

own.pop_provenance: historical demography c.1770 (pre-1st-partition ~12M); standard estimate, tech-debt to exact Maddison pop

adversaries.gdppc_provenance: longrun_pillars.json RUS P4_gdp nearest=1860 (no 1772 value; flag year-gap, Russian power was demographic not per-capita)
adversaries.pop_provenance: Russian Empire c.1770 ~25M, standard historical demography

adversaries.gdppc_provenance: longrun_pillars.json DEU P4_gdp @1772 (DEU as Prussia proxy)

adversaries.pop_provenance: Habsburg monarchy c.1770 ~18M, standard historical demography

E1_relative_power.detail: Commonwealth economic mass vs the JOINT mass of its three partitioning neighbors. Mass = GDPpc x pop. Own ~11,688; joint adversary ~61,800 (Russia ~18,850 + Prussia ~8,020 + Austria ~34,938) -> overwhelming.
E1_relative_power.provenance: Maddison GDPpc (repo) x historical-demography population (supplied). HISTORICAL-PROXY.

E2_patron.detail: No external guarantor; the three neighbors WERE the predators. Documented historical fact (no ATOP pre-1816).

E3_contested_border.detail: Active partitionist designs by all three neighbors (First Partition Aug 1772). Documented historical fact (no ICOW pre-1816).

E4_neighborhood.detail: Surrounded by three hostile great powers; Russo-Turkish war + Bar Confederation context. Documented historical fact.

E5_great_power_faultline.detail: The Commonwealth WAS the contested ground between three rising absolutist powers.

R4_strategic_depth.provenance: Commonwealth area c.1772 ~730k km2 (large, but no mobilizational capacity to use it - the depth is nominal).
R4_strategic_depth.note: Large area, but depth without capacity. The R2 (P1) read is what carries the response signal, and it is very low (rol 0.18).

Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth@1772.outcome_factual: Three partitions (1772, 1793, 1795); the state was erased from the map until 1918.
Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth@1772.demonstrates: The SAME logic as citable-tier Cyprus (high exposure + no patron + collapsed relative power -> erasure), but at the historical-proxy confidence tier. Real Maddison/V-Dem data, NOT interpretation.
